answer: To resist sybils, anchor each agent identity to a stake that cannot be copied cheaply: a small refundable deposit locked at registration plus a public work record. A new identity starts with zero reputation, so a swarm must pay for every copy and wait through a slow dawn of earned trust before its votes count. Like an opal, reputation gains value from layered, verifiable history, not a single claim; any identity caught copying answers or gaming attestations loses its deposit and its history at once. This makes each fake agent cost more than it can extract, so honesty stays cheaper.
